newsitem.title: RUSSIA: SOCCER-SPARTAK MOSCOW WIN 4-3 TO GO TOP WITH TWO GAMES LEFT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SPARTAK MOSCOW WIN 4-3 TO GO TOP WITH TWO GAMES LEFT.

text.p: Spartak Moscow came from 3-1 down to win 4-3 at rivals Torpedo Moscow on Sunday and went top of the Russian league by one point -- setting up a nail-biting climax to the season with just two games to go.
Spartak are now on 68 points, one ahead of Rotor Volgograd who stumbled to a disappointing 0-0 draw at strugglers Chernomorets Novorossiisk on Saturday.
Defending champions Alania Vladikavkaz ensured they stayed in the hunt by beating bottom side Lada Togliatti 3-0 to go third with 66 points.
Torpedo's Vyacheslav Kamoltsev started the game superbly and when he notched his second long-range goal in the 29th minute to make the score 3-1, Spartak looked doomed.

But Dmitry Alenichev pulled a goal back after the break and Andrei Tikhonov equalised with a penalty in the 77th minute before forward Vyacheslav Dubanov scored a dramatic winner with just 10 minutes left.
Spartak, who have lost many of the players who won them the Russian championship three years running in 1992-94, are not guaranteed the title yet.
Next week they host mid-table Rostselmash Rostov while Alania travel to struggling Tekstilshchik Kamyshin, who are almost certain to be relegated.
Rotor, who have looked increasingly nervous of late, have the toughest match -- away at sixth place Lokomotiv Moscow.
CSKA Moscow, who started the weekend third on 63 points, effectively ruled themselves out of the title race by losing 2-1 at mid-table Baltika Kaliningrad.
Dynamo Moscow's hopes of sneaking the title also vanished thanks to a 3-2 defeat at KamAZ Naberezhniye Chelny.
